experiments.title: Structured Memory Handoff Test
experiments.hypothesis: Explicit structured project memory improves handoff fidelity over a flat baseline without increasing critical fabrications.
experiments.metric: PCRB-1 score, paired delta and critical fabrication count
experiments.acceptance_rule: Pilot: three paired trials and mean structured improvement >= 10 with lower 95% bound > 5; final adoption additionally requires nine paired trials, model/provider diversity, holdout, calibration and regression pass.
experiments.notes: Pilot adjudicated REJECT on a critical fabrication confirmed by two evaluators (2026-09-16). Its +24.2 gap is not evidence about structure: the two states carried different facts and the structured state leaked its condition label. See PILOT_DESIGN_FLAWS.md. Superseded by PROP-EXP-MEM-002.

experiments.title: Independent Evaluator Reliability Test
experiments.hypothesis: Two evaluator models from different providers can score the same blinded outputs with bounded disagreement and explicit fabrication reconciliation.
experiments.metric: within-pair absolute score difference, fabrication agreement and calibration pass rate
experiments.acceptance_rule: At least two independent evaluators, disagreement <= 15 points on every pair, no unresolved calibration failure, and no unconfirmed fabrication treated as a rejection.
experiments.notes: This is registered as proposed; it has not been run.

experiments.title: Canonical State Regression Preservation
experiments.hypothesis: A candidate memory or evaluator change can improve the target metric without degrading mission reconstruction, failure preservation or next-action fidelity.
experiments.metric: fixed regression scorecard across multiple capabilities
experiments.acceptance_rule: Every registered capability meets its minimum threshold; any failed capability vetoes final adoption.
experiments.notes: Failure vetoes the candidate; it does not silently rewrite canonical history.

experiments.title: Structure-only Memory Handoff Test
experiments.hypothesis: Holding information content constant, a sectioned project state improves blind handoff fidelity over the same facts in prose, without increasing critical fabrications.
experiments.metric: PCRB-1 score, paired delta and critical fabrication count
experiments.acceptance_rule: V4 gate, pilot stage: nine paired trials, single generator identity; best outcome PROVISIONAL_KEEP.
experiments.notes: Adjudicated REJECT on 2026-09-16: one critical fabrication confirmed in each condition. Hypothesis not supported: structured scored lower for both scorers (-4.4 and -2.1 mean paired delta, not significant). See RESULT.md. Followed by PROP-EXP-MEM-003.

experiments.title: Structure-only Handoff with a Capable Generator
experiments.hypothesis: Holding information content constant, a sectioned project state improves blind handoff fidelity over the same facts in prose, without increasing critical fabrications, for a capable hosted generator.
experiments.metric: PCRB-2 score (components only, totals computed), paired delta and confirmed critical fabrications per condition
experiments.acceptance_rule: V4 gate, pilot stage, ADR-004 options: thirty pairs; REJECT if structured has more confirmed fabrications, mean improvement < 10 or lower 95% bound <= 5; INCONCLUSIVE if scorers disagree by > 15 on more than 20% of pairs; best outcome PROVISIONAL_KEEP.
experiments.notes: Same inputs as MEM-002; generator qwen/qwen3.8-27b on Groq; pre-registered scorer and checker ladders; runs unattended through scripts/run_experiment.py.

experiments.title: Handoff Quiz: Structure Measured Without a Judge
experiments.hypothesis: Holding information content constant, a sectioned project state transfers more correct facts through a handoff than the same facts in prose, without more invented facts.
experiments.metric: Fact accuracy on 32 keyed questions answered by a reader from the handoff alone (paired delta, percentage points); inventions on 10 questions about absent facts
experiments.acceptance_rule: Thirty pairs. REJECT if structured inventions exceed baseline by more than 5; PROVISIONAL_KEEP if mean delta >= +10 pp and 95% lower bound > 0; REJECT if 95% upper bound < +10 pp; else INCONCLUSIVE.
experiments.notes: REJECT on 2026-09-17: mean paired delta -0.9 pp, 95% CI -4.1 to +2.2 pp, zero inventions and zero wrong facts in both conditions. See RESULT.md.

experiments.title: Handoff Checklist
experiments.hypothesis: A short generic checklist of the state's item kinds, added after the state, increases the facts a reader recovers from the handoff without more invented facts.
experiments.metric: Fact accuracy on 32 keyed questions from the handoff alone (paired delta, pp); inventions on 10 absent-fact questions
experiments.acceptance_rule: Thirty pairs. REJECT if checklist inventions exceed baseline by more than 5; PROVISIONAL_KEEP if mean delta >= +5 pp and 95% lower bound > 0; REJECT if 95% upper bound < +5 pp; else INCONCLUSIVE.
experiments.notes: INCONCLUSIVE on 2026-09-18: +4.1 pp (95% CI +1.5 to +6.6), below the pre-registered +5 pp bar but excluding zero; zero inventions in both conditions. First positive signal of the project. See RESULT.md.

experiments.title: Handoff Checklist, Replication with Other Models
experiments.hypothesis: The handoff checklist raises fact transfer by at least 5 points with a generator and a reader from families not used before.
experiments.metric: Fact accuracy on 32 keyed questions from the handoff alone (paired delta, pp); inventions on 10 absent-fact questions
experiments.acceptance_rule: Sixty pairs, rule identical to MEM-005: REJECT if inventions exceed baseline by more than 5; PROVISIONAL_KEEP if mean delta >= +5 pp and 95% lower bound > 0; REJECT if 95% upper bound < +5 pp; else INCONCLUSIVE.
experiments.notes: PROVISIONAL_KEEP on 2026-09-19 with an independent reader: +5.9 pp (95% CI +3.5 to +8.2), zero inventions. The ladder's fallback reader was the generator itself; that reading is published but set aside (D3). A DeepSeek cross-read gave +5.1. See RESULT.md.

experiments.title: Handoff Checklist, Third Generator Family
experiments.hypothesis: The handoff checklist raises fact transfer by at least 5 points when a DeepSeek generator writes the handoffs and MEM-005's reader model reads them.
experiments.metric: Fact accuracy on 32 keyed questions from the handoff alone (paired delta, pp); inventions on 10 absent-fact questions
experiments.acceptance_rule: Sixty pairs, rule identical to MEM-005 and MEM-006: REJECT if inventions exceed baseline by more than 5; PROVISIONAL_KEEP if mean delta >= +5 pp and 95% lower bound > 0; REJECT if 95% upper bound < +5 pp; else INCONCLUSIVE.
experiments.notes: PROVISIONAL_KEEP on 2026-09-19: +5.5 pp (95% CI +3.8 to +7.3), 46 pairs better of 60, zero inventions. Third writer family. First paid run, about 0.20 USD under a 0.50 ceiling. See RESULT.md.

experiments.title: Handoff Chains: How Fast a Project Decays
experiments.hypothesis: Across repeated handoffs, an instruction naming the kinds of item to carry preserves more facts than a free summary, at equal length, on documents from unrelated domains, without more invented facts.
experiments.metric: Fact accuracy from the handoff alone at hops 1, 3 and 5 (paired against the control strategy); inventions on absent-fact questions
experiments.acceptance_rule: At hop 3 the checklist must keep at least 10 pp more facts than the summary with the 95% lower bound above 0, on at least two of three documents; rejected if it invents more by over 5.
experiments.notes: Rule satisfied on all three documents: +31.9, +16.7 and +20.8 pp at hop 3, zero inventions in 1152 absent-fact answers. Loss happens almost entirely at the first handoff and the chain then holds: a free summary drops a third of the document immediately. Cost 1.30 USD. See RESULT.md.

experiments.title: Continuity Programme, Stage 1: Populations versus Lineages
experiments.hypothesis: Merging several independent chains recovers a large part of what each lost, because they lost different facts.
experiments.metric: Fact accuracy of a merged handoff against the mean and the best of its source chains
experiments.acceptance_rule: At least 15 pp above the sources' mean with the 95% lower bound above 0, on at least two of three documents, without inventing more than 5.
experiments.notes: Refused as registered: +11.6, +6.9 and +1.4 pp, and no merge beat the best single chain at equal length. Zero inventions. Exploratory follow-up at double the budget exceeds the best chain on two documents of three, and fails on the one whose chains had almost nothing to reconcile. See RESULT.md.

experiments.title: Memory against Archive: Can a Chain Recover What It Lost?
experiments.hypothesis: A chain of handoffs that may consult a verifiable archive - an index of hashed entries, with a narrow retrieval channel - keeps substantially more facts at hop 5 than a chain that can only remember.
experiments.metric: Fact accuracy from the handoff alone at hops 1, 3 and 5, paired against the bare regime; identifiers retrieved at each hop; inventions on absent-fact questions
experiments.acceptance_rule: At hop 5 the anchored regime must keep at least 20 pp more facts than the bare regime with the paired 95% lower bound above 0, on at least two of three documents. The middle arm (index only, no retrieval) decides how the result is named; both namings are fixed in PROTOCOL.md before the run.
experiments.notes: Refused as registered, and the rule could not have been met: the control kept 93.8-95.8 %% of facts, so the largest available effect was +4.2 to +6.2 points against a +20 threshold. The defect was building the archive arms on the best instruction found so far. Both archive regimes cost 1.4 to 3.6 points rather than gaining. Zero inventions in 432 absent-fact answers, no failed run in 54 chains, and the control reproduces MEM-008's checklist arm in a harness written separately. Retested with headroom in PROP-EXP-MEM-011.

experiments.title: Memory against Archive, with Room to Lose
experiments.hypothesis: A chain that may consult a verifiable archive keeps substantially more facts at hop 5 than one that can only remember, when the chain is losing enough for an archive to matter.
experiments.metric: Fact accuracy from the handoff alone at hops 1, 3 and 5, paired against the bare regime; identifiers retrieved at each hop; inventions on absent-fact questions
experiments.acceptance_rule: At hop 5 the anchored regime must keep at least 20 pp more facts than the bare regime with the paired 95% lower bound above 0, on at least two of three documents. As in MEM-010, the index-only arm decides how a positive result is named, and both namings are fixed before the run.
experiments.notes: Stage 2 of the Continuity Programme, retested. MEM-010 refused its rule with no power to pass it; this run uses the free summary instruction, whose hop-5 scores of 61.6, 79.9 and 70.1 % leave 20 to 38 points of headroom. Threshold unchanged from docs/CONTINUITY_PROGRAMME.md.
